title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A 'type' G is a combinatorial type of stable marked curve, essentially a dual graph. Â is its set of 'arêtes': nodes together with the free marked points I. M_G is the holomorphic multiplicity (orbifold/stack) of curves of type G. C ⊂ Â is a set of nodes, and G' is the type obtained by smoothing ('chirurgie holomorphe') the nodes in C.

Previous page.
- M^C_G is the multiplicity of pairs (X, (D_x)), where the D_x are disjoint holomorphic discs at the two branches of each node x ∈ C. The forgetful map M^C_G → M_G is a homotopy equivalence.
- Over M^C_G sits a U^C-torsor M̃^C_G, where U is the circle group. Its fibre is the set of choices t = (t_x), with each t_x an anti-isomorphism of the two boundary circles of X minus its discs. It is the pull-back of the torsor P_C of unit vectors of the plumbing lines T_{x'} ⊗ T_{x''}, x ∈ C.
- Gluing along the t_x gives a morphism of topoi M̃^C_G → M_{G'}.

This page.
- Over M_{G'} take the principal U^{Â'}-bundle SP_{G'}. Its fibre at X' is T_{X'} = ∏_{x∈Â'} T_{X',x}, with T_{X',x} defined as before.
 - For a node, T_{X',x} is the unit part of the tensor product of the branch tangents.
 - For a marked point x ∈ I', it is the unit tangent torsor (T_{X',x} − 0)/R^{*+}.
- Define ST_{G'} := π_1(SP_{G'}). For G' smooth this is the fundamental group of the moduli of curves with real tangential base points at the marked points. That is the mapping class group of a surface with boundary circles, a central extension by Z^{I'} of Γ_{g,n}. In general it is π_1 of the torus bundle of unit 'normal' directions over the stratum M_{G'}.
- For G, split Â = C ⊔ B. Let P_B be the U^B-torsor over M_G. Then SP_G = P_C ×_{M_G} P_B as U^Â-torsors.
- Form the cube: the bottom face is P_C → M_G ← P_B with SP_G as fibre product. The top face is its base change along the homotopy equivalence M^C_G → M_G. The top-face spaces are M̃^C_G ≃ pull-back of P_C, P^B_G = P_B ×_{M_G} M^C_G, and P̃^B_G = M̃^C_G ×_{M_G} P_B.
- Since the base change is a homotopy equivalence, all vertical arrows are homotopy equivalences. Hence (next page) ST̃_G := π_1(SP_G) ≃ π_1(P̃^B_G).

Next page. A cartesian square P̃^B_G → SP_{G'} over M̃^C_G → M_{G'} yields the 'gluing' homomorphism ST̃_G → ST_{G'}. The monoid ]0,1]^C, acting by shrinking the discs, is then introduced to compare with the degeneration to the node.

In modern terms, this is the construction of the inclusion of the stabilizer of a multicurve, including the boundary Dehn twists Z^C, into the mapping class group of the glued surface. It is realised as π_1 of the unit normal torus bundle of a boundary stratum (a real oriented blow-up) mapping to the open moduli space via plumbing. This supplies the morphisms of the Teichmüller tower along contractions of stable graphs, as in the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors:
No substantive error. Two points are left implicit.
- Homotopy equivalence of M^C_G → M_G. The fibre is a space of disjoint holomorphic discs (or local coordinates); it is contractible by dilation, but this is not argued.
- Compatibility of the anti-isomorphisms t_x with P_C. The previous page notes that M̃^C_G is the pull-back of P_C; the identification of the U^C-actions, including the orientation conventions for an anti-isomorphism versus the tensor line T_{x'}⊗T_{x''}, is asserted rather than checked.
Notation is inconsistent: 'U^B_B' must mean U^B over M_G, and C counts nodes, not half-edges. Otherwise SP_G = P_C ×_{M_G} P_B would not be a U^Â-torsor.

ideas.what: ST_G := π_1 of the principal U^{Â}-bundle of unit tangent / unit plumbing directions over the stratum M_G (tangential base points at marked points and nodes)
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group of the real oriented blow-up boundary stratum; mapping class group of a surface with boundary / multicurve stabilizer with boundary twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov (1995) and Looijenga for real blow-ups of M̄_{g,n}; Ihara–Nakamura for boundary maps of fundamental groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower and gluing operations informally, without this torsor formalism

ideas.what: Holomorphic surgery (plumbing) via anti-isomorphisms of boundary circles gives a morphism M̃^C_G → M_{G'}, and hence ST̃_G → ST_{G'}
ideas.modern_name: plumbing construction / gluing maps of the Teichmüller (modular) operad
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fay, Earle–Marden, Wolpert (plumbing); Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads); Bakalov–Kirillov and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (Teichmüller groupoids)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches it

ideas.what: Base change along the homotopy equivalence M^C_G → M_G makes all vertical arrows homotopy equivalences, giving π_1(SP_G) ≃ π_1(P̃^B_G)
ideas.modern_name: homotopy invariance under contractible choices of coordinates

missed.claim: Grothendieck uniformly attaches to every stratum type G a group π_1 of a U^{Â}-torsor of unit tangent and unit plumbing directions, with gluing homomorphisms along graph contractions. This is effectively the real-oriented-blow-up / modular-operad picture of mapping class groups, with tangential base points at nodes treated like those at marked points, formulated at the level of holomorphic multiplicities. It predates the Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov and Getzler–Kapranov formalisms, but the content is now standard.
missed.quote: on considère le fibré SP_{G'} sur M_{G'}, principal de groupe U^{Â'} ... S T_{G'} = π_1(SP_{G'})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that Grothendieck's Teichmüller tower was intended as a functor on stable graphs, built from unit normal torus bundles of strata, i.e. a modular-operad structure.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but essentially routine construction of the gluing homomorphisms between Teichmüller groups using tangential base points and plumbing; equivalent constructions are well established in the later literature. Its interest is historical: an early, uniform torsor-theoretic formulation.

Middle of the diagram: the entries are P̃^B_G and P^B_G, with dashed arrows indicating base change of P_B.
'groupe structural U^B_B' should read U^B (over M_G).
'T_{\cdot}^{*}{}_{X',x}' should read T_{X',x} minus 0, i.e. (T_{X',x} − 0)/R^{*+}, the unit tangent torsor.
